evidence: 6 slides taken from the public photo page in the browser pane (gallery-dl returned nothing, yt-dlp got the sound only). Visual numbers from measures.json; boxes estimated from the slides and checked with measure.py check.

fingerprint.structure: 6 slides: hook macro with a 3-word reveal (lips) -> one normal selfie that shows the whole person -> 3 silent extreme skin macros of the same face (eye, nose in profile, cheek) -> a last macro (brow and forehead) carrying the comment-keyword CTA
fingerprint.hook: reveal-by-claim: 'this is AI' over the most convincing extreme close-up, so the viewer's eye has already accepted it as a photo before reading the line (disbelief mechanic). AI is the only bold word
fingerprint.camera_motion: humans. Slide 2 is a selfie (term 1, no phone in shot) of one young woman in a red hood, outdoors under a porch in flat daylight, arms folded at her chest. Slides 1, 3 to 6 are extreme macro phone-camera close-ups of the same face, filling the frame edge to edge, shallow focus with the edges falling soft, flat daylight, same red hood visible at the edges for continuity
fingerprint.pacing: text on 2 of 6 slides only (3 words on slide 1, 10 words on slide 6); slides 2 to 5 have no text, the texture is the content
fingerprint.text_overlay: clean white geometric sans (closest Montserrat), light/regular weight with the key word in bold, sentence case in the source, centred in the frame, no box, no outline, no visible shadow, size about 3.3% of the height on slide 1 and 2.3% on slide 6
fingerprint.audio: trending instrumental beat ('Thewayyouare', BYDKA BEATS), not the creator's own sound
fingerprint.arc: claim -> context (the whole person, looks like any selfie) -> escalating proof (closer and closer skin detail) -> action (comment keyword). The payoff is the viewer failing to find the AI
